Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with long-term chromatin accessibility tracking (ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief pulse of a stimulus (e.g., serum, TNF, or injury) that activates AP-1 (FOS/JUN), then wash it out and profile accessibility and AP-1 binding by ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN at days to weeks. Persistence of AP-1-motif-containing open regions, like a 'spookology' of ghost marks left after the stimulus is gone, would show a lasting memory footprint. Naive and pulsed cells give the baseline comparison.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation at defined times (degron, dominant-negative A-FOS)
ideas.description: Use a degron-tagged JUN/FOS or inducible A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during the stimulus, or after the stimulus has ended. If accessibility and faster re-induction persist after post-stimulus AP-1 loss, the memory is self-sustained by chromatin. If they decay, AP-1 is continuously required to maintain it. Comparing the two timings separates initiation from maintenance.

ideas.title: Priming and re-stimulation transcriptional response assay
ideas.description: Give two stimulus pulses separated by a rest interval of varying length, and measure nascent transcription (PRO-seq or EU-seq) and target-gene RNA after the second pulse. Faster or stronger induction in primed cells than in naive cells, at AP-1 target genes only, would indicate memory. The decay time of this enhanced response quantifies memory duration. AP-1 knockdown before priming tests necessity.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and live reporter lineage tracing
ideas.description: Combine single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing with live-cell imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter (or endogenous tagged FOS) across cell divisions. Track whether daughter cells inherit the primed state, which would show mitotic heritability. Use the data to ask whether memory is a bistable, all-or-none state or a graded one, and to find cell-to-cell variability in it.

ideas.title: Sufficiency test by targeted AP-1 recruitment plus histone/DNA-methylation readouts
ideas.description: Recruit JUN or FOS to a synthetic reporter or a chosen enhancer with dCas9 or a Gal4 system for a limited time, then release it and watch the reporter over many cell divisions. Pair this with ChIP or CUT&Tag for H3K27ac and H3K4me1 and with methylation profiling, and test cooperation with the SWI/SNF (BAF) complex using a BRG1 inhibitor. Persistent activity and marks after release would show that AP-1 alone is sufficient to set a memory state. A lack of persistence would show that it is not.
